title: Brewers win first World Series in franchise history, beating Rays 4-1 in Game 5
excerpt: Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 4-1 in Game 5 on October 28 to win its first World Series, capping an 11-2 October run for baseball's smallest-market team.
content:
After 58 seasons, the Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions. Milwaukee beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night, October 28, at Tropicana Field, closing out the series four games to one and ending the franchise's long wait.

Second-year ace Jacob Misiorowski delivered the clincher, throwing 5 2/3 scoreless innings before leaving with a leg cramp, and catcher William Contreras was named World Series MVP after batting .381 with four RBIs in the series. Rookie Cooper Pratt drove in two runs in Game 5, and Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits.

The title caps a dominant season: Milwaukee won a franchise-record 103 regular-season games, then went 11-2 in October, dethroning the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers along the way. The Brewers play in Major League Baseball's smallest market and carried only the 19th-highest payroll — a small-market champion in a winter when a lockout is widely expected as owners push for a salary cap.

The franchise began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee in 1970. Its only previous World Series trip, in 1982, ended in a Game 7 loss to St. Louis. Game 4 of this series nearly extended the wait further — Tampa Bay won a 12-inning thriller — but Milwaukee answered the next night in front of thousands of traveling fans.

For Laredo readers, the local angle is a familiar one: a border city knows what it means to be counted out by size. Milwaukee just proved, again, that payroll and market size do not decide October — pitching, defense and a roster that refuses to blink do.
